Instead of sending them elsewhere, bring Glean's answers into the app they
already use — with permissions enforced per user, automatically.

Scope chat to a specific agent by passing its `agentId` to the chat component.

https://developers.glean.com/cookbook/embed-search-chat

recipes.title: Draft PR reviews with Glean Triggers and Claude Code Monitor
recipes.description: Use Glean Triggers to send GitHub review events to Claude Code Monitor, which runs your local review skill against the diff and prepares a first-pass review draft.
prerequisites: Glean Triggers enabled with GitHub review presets available in your deployment
GitHub content indexed in Glean
A local checkout of the repository, with the GitHub CLI signed in as the reviewer
An interactive Claude Code session, or the terminal stream where Monitor is unavailable
Node 20+ and a public HTTPS tunnel to the receiver

demoQueries.expectedBehavior: One signed event reaches the receiver and Claude drafts a review of the current diff. Nothing is posted to GitHub.

demoQueries.expectedBehavior: The helper creates or updates a pending review and reports that it remains unsubmitted.

codeAssets.description: Signed webhook receiver, durable monitor queue, Claude Code plugin, fixture test, and pending-review helper

steps.title: Verify the local path with no credentials
steps.description: Use recorded events to verify the signed receiver, event queue, and draft-review flow.

steps.title: Sign in to Glean
steps.description: Sign in to discover your tenant and save GLEAN_SERVER_URL and GLEAN_API_TOKEN to the ignored .env file. An exported GLEAN_API_TOKEN takes precedence over .env, and the scripts warn you when it does.

steps.title: Run the receiver
steps.description: Keep the receiver running. It listens on loopback, verifies signatures, and queues each webhook ID once.

steps.title: Expose the receiver over HTTPS
steps.description: Append /webhook to the printed origin and set GLEAN_WEBHOOK_URL before registering. Keep the tunnel running: triggers outlive the tunnel, so closing it sends future deliveries to a dead address.

steps.title: Register the review triggers
steps.description: Set GLEAN_TRIGGER_DATASOURCE and the preset IDs to register. If you leave the IDs empty, setup lists the presets available in your deployment and stops instead of guessing. Provide required preset inputs through GLEAN_TRIGGER_INPUT_<FIELD>.

steps.title: Attach Claude Code Monitor
steps.description: Validate the plugin, then restart Claude Code from the repository under review so Monitor starts with the session. If Monitor is unavailable, run npm run stream to receive the same events in the terminal.

steps.title: Verify a real review request
steps.description: Request a review from yourself on a real pull request. Confirm one queued event and one draft grounded in the current diff. The workflow makes no GitHub write until you ask for one.

questions.prompt: What is your work email? It is used once to discover your Glean tenant.
Which local GitHub repository should Claude Code review?
Which public HTTPS URL should receive Glean webhook delivery? If you do not have one, say so and the tunnel step prints one.

verification.expectedDuration: under 1 minute for signed fixture delivery; 5–15 minutes for a live indexed event

run.url: the Local URL printed by the receiver

architecture.label: Local receiver + Monitor
architecture.caption: Verifies, deduplicates, queues, and wakes Claude Code

architecture.label: Pending GitHub review
architecture.caption: Human inspects and decides whether to submit

content.problem:
You already have the repository, local diff, and review tools in Claude Code. The hard part is noticing a new review request and rebuilding enough context to give it a thoughtful first pass.

Glean catches the GitHub event and delivers it to Claude Code Monitor, where your local review skill examines the current diff and prepares initial findings. You review and refine the draft, then decide whether anything should be submitted.
takeItFurther: Teach the local review skill your repository's conventions and test commands, so the first pass reflects how your team already reviews.
Notify the reviewer when the first-pass draft is ready, so the queue is not something anyone has to remember to check.
Add inline pending-review comments once the body-only flow is reliable — line-level findings are what a reviewer acts on first.

guardrails.title: Draft is not submit
guardrails.rule: The monitor may prepare a local draft. A GitHub pending review requires explicit approval, and submission always remains manual.

guardrails.title: Event payload is not the diff
guardrails.rule: Review the current local repository and GitHub head SHA; never infer findings from the thin trigger payload alone.

limitations.title: Claude Code Monitor requires an interactive host
limitations.description: Monitor requires a supported interactive Claude Code session. Where Monitor is unavailable, use the terminal stream to receive the same events.

recipes.aiPrompt: Scaffold the shipped receiver and Claude Code plugin. For trigger concepts or endpoint details, consult https://developers.glean.com/guides/triggers/overview and https://developers.glean.com/api/platform-api/triggers-overview. Run the fixture test before requesting credentials. Use the shipped login flow, start the receiver, create a public HTTPS tunnel, and store only the URL and returned secrets in ignored .env. Register the GitHub review presets selected from the deployment's live catalog. If none of the required review-event presets is available, stop rather than inventing an id. Validate and load the plugin in an interactive session opened in the target repository. Preserve the local-draft-first boundary: create a pending GitHub review only after explicit approval, and never submit it.
recipes.llmContext: Delivery uses Standard Webhooks, at-least-once. Payload is flat snake_case, no wrapper: version, trigger_id, event_type, datasource, reason, doc_type, doc_id, view_url, title, event_time; webhook-id exists only in headers. Verify HMAC over the raw bytes, since re-serialising changes the signature; reject stale timestamps and deduplicate webhook-id. Every Triggers request needs x-glean-include-experimental: true, or the API answers 401 Not allowed. A 401 on a valid TRIGGERS-scoped token means the grant was revoked: sign in again. events/search looks backward; delivery fires forward from trigger creation. PATCH /triggers/{id} re-points delivery.webhook_url and keeps the signing secret, issued once, so a fresh checkout cannot adopt existing triggers. Diffs come from gh, matching the head SHA. A pending review is author-only; never approve, request changes, or submit it.

prerequisites: Glean Triggers enabled with the Gong preset available, Gong calls indexed, and credentials scoped for Triggers, Search, and Chat
A publicly reachable n8n instance, or a local one exposed with npx n8n start --tunnel
Permission to install the Glean n8n community nodes

demoQueries.query: Finish a Gong call involving the trigger owner and a customer with a matching Salesforce Account
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: The workflow summarizes the call, creates one completed Salesforce activity on the matched Account, and posts the summary and source link to the configured Slack destination.

codeAssets.description: Importable n8n workflow plus an offline structural verifier

steps.title: Choose n8n hosting before scaffolding
steps.description: Choose n8n Cloud or local/self-hosted n8n before downloading anything. Cloud is public by default. Local/self-hosted needs a public HTTPS webhook origin—use n8n's development `--tunnel`, Cloudflare Tunnel, or another ingress, and keep it available before publishing.

steps.title: Resolve the Glean backend
steps.description: Run the cookbook resolver with the work email. It may see a legacy frontend address such as `*.askscio.com`, but it returns the API backend `https://<instance>-be.glean.com`. Use that result for Glean Chat; do not paste the discovery address into the workflow.

steps.title: Install the Glean n8n nodes
steps.description: In n8n, open Settings → Community nodes → Install and add `@gleanwork/n8n-nodes-gleanclient@0.4.2`. It provides the Trigger and Search nodes; the workflow uses an HTTP Request for Chat. Cloud works as shipped. For self-hosted n8n, set the webhook base to your public origin or start the development tunnel.

steps.title: Import the workflow
steps.description: In n8n, choose Workflows → Import from File and select the scaffolded `workflow.json`; this is the route that keeps your local edits. Import from URL always fetches the untouched GitHub file. If your browser cannot see the scaffolded file, copy and paste it onto a blank canvas. Confirm that the ten nodes and Start here note appear.

steps.title: Attach credentials
steps.description: Attach a Glean Trigger credential with `TRIGGERS`, a Glean Client credential with `SEARCH` and `CHAT`, plus your Salesforce and Slack credentials. The trigger follows the Glean credential owner; there is no separate user to select.

steps.title: Configure Glean Chat and Slack routing
steps.description: Set the Glean Chat node to the backend returned by the resolver, then choose one reviewed Slack channel or an Account-to-channel map. n8n Variables can hold the backend and routing values, but they are optional.

steps.title: Verify the workflow with no credentials
steps.description: Run the fixture verifier against recorded data. If you edited the local workflow.json, run `npm run verify:config` too. That command cannot see values entered in the n8n UI or stored in n8n Variables, so verify those configurations inside n8n before publishing.

steps.title: Publish the workflow
steps.description: Publish the workflow in n8n. The Glean Trigger node registers the production webhook and stores the signing secret used to verify deliveries.

steps.title: Verify with a real Gong call
steps.description: Make a short Gong call with yourself as a participant. Confirm one execution, one completed Salesforce activity on the matched Account, and one Slack post. Read the summary before widening the audience.

questions.prompt: Will you use n8n Cloud or a local/self-hosted n8n instance? If local/self-hosted, choose a public HTTPS option before importing: n8n's development --tunnel, Cloudflare Tunnel, or another public ingress. Glean cannot deliver to localhost.
What is your work email? It is used once to discover your Glean tenant and normalized API backend.
Where should the follow-up go in Slack? Start with one channel id, or provide a Salesforce Account id → Slack channel id map if each account team has its own destination. Use ids, not names.

verification.expectedDuration: 5–15 minutes after a test Gong call is indexed

architecture.label: Gong
architecture.caption: A new indexed call involving you

architecture.label: Glean Trigger
architecture.caption: Delivers the call securely to n8n

architecture.label: n8n
architecture.caption: Finds context, writes the summary, and matches one account

architecture.label: Salesforce + Slack
architecture.caption: Records the activity and shares the right update

content.problem:
Important follow-up gets lost after customer calls—not because the information is missing, but because it is scattered across Gong, Salesforce, and Slack.

This recipe connects those systems in n8n. When a new Gong call is indexed, Glean finds permission-aware context and summarizes it, Salesforce gets an activity only when one account matches, and Slack receives a focused update for the right audience.
takeItFurther: Create Salesforce follow-up tasks from explicit call action items, so every commitment has an owner.
Send a daily digest of completed and unresolved follow-ups instead of one Slack post per call.
Route unresolved accounts to a human review queue once that ownership path is in place.

guardrails.title: One account or no write
guardrails.rule: The workflow writes only after exactly one Salesforce Account matches. Ambiguity stops the run instead of choosing for you.

guardrails.title: Evidence before summary
guardrails.rule: The summary uses the call and permission-aware Glean results. Unsupported commitments, dates, and pricing stay out.

limitations.title: Account matching still needs a review path
limitations.description: Glean Chat proposes the customer from the call context, but Salesforce remains the authority. The workflow continues only when exactly one Account matches; otherwise it stops for resolution.

recipes.aiPrompt: Before downloading the workflow, ask whether the user will use n8n Cloud or local/self-hosted n8n. For local/self-hosted, require a public HTTPS webhook origin before publishing; offer n8n's development --tunnel, Cloudflare Tunnel, or another public ingress, and never accept localhost as reachable by Glean. Ask for the user's work email, then run the cookbook plugin's resolve-backend.mjs script and use its normalized https://<instance>-be.glean.com result for the Glean Chat URL; do not paste a legacy *.askscio.com discovery URL into the workflow. For trigger concepts or endpoint details, consult https://developers.glean.com/guides/triggers/overview and https://developers.glean.com/api/platform-api/triggers-overview. Scaffold the shipped n8n workflow, install exactly @gleanwork/n8n-nodes-gleanclient@0.4.2, and attach host-managed credentials rather than writing secrets into JSON. Keep the live Glean preset selected by semantics, not only by cached id. Configure either one reviewed central Slack destination or a reviewed Account-to-channel map. Preserve the single-account gate and the completed Salesforce activity pattern. Run the offline workflow verifier, publish only after every credential and mapping is configured, then verify one real Gong call end to end.
recipes.llmContext: The published Glean n8n package is 0.4.2. It includes a Glean Trigger node and a Glean Search action, not a Glean Chat node. The trigger registers POST /api/triggers on activation, stores the returned signing secret, verifies Standard Webhooks delivery, and deletes the trigger on deactivation. Glean event payloads are thin, so retrieve permission-aware context before summarization. n8n credentials must remain host-managed. Do not write to Salesforce or Slack if the account is absent, ambiguous, or unsupported by evidence.

recipes.title: Multi-step agent with governed tools
recipes.description: Build a Glean agent that plans, retrieves, and acts through a governed custom tool — with a safe fallback when the tool is denied.
prerequisites: Agent builder access in your Glean instance
Permission to register a custom tool (or admin help)
A work email for tenant discovery and OAuth sign-in; an AGENTS-scoped API token is the fallback
uv and cloudflared installed locally
Your own email, to put on (and take off) the tool server's allow-list between the two runs

demoQueries.query: Summarize our open incidents and file a tracking ticket
demoQueries.expectedBehavior: With your email on the tool server's allow-list: the agent summarizes and the demo tool call succeeds (200, a fake in-memory ticket id). With it removed: the tool returns 403 and the agent falls back to a read-only summary rather than failing the run. The allow-list demonstrates authorization logic; authenticate requests from Glean before connecting a real write action.

codeAssets.description: Governed custom Tool — files an incident ticket, restricted to one group
Invoke the agent via agents.run, demo both the permitted and denied branches

steps.title: Set the tool server's allow-list
steps.description: Set AUTHORIZED_EMAILS to your own email for the first run. You'll remove it for the second run to see the denied branch — changing the allow-list is how both governance paths get demonstrated, since the agent always runs as you. The server refuses to start on an empty allow-list, since that denies everyone and makes the permitted branch unobservable.

steps.title: Run the tool server
steps.description: Listens on port 8080. Keep this running in its own terminal — the agent calls it over HTTP once registered.

steps.title: Expose the demo tool over HTTPS
steps.description: Keep this running in a second terminal. Copy the printed https://<random>.trycloudflare.com origin into tool-server/openapi.yaml as servers[0].url, with no path. Confirm that <origin>/file_incident_ticket returns the expected 403 for a denied email. This public demo route accepts a spoofable identity header and only creates fake in-memory tickets; authenticate requests from Glean before connecting a real write action.

steps.title: Register the tool
steps.description: Manual, UI-only step. After replacing the OpenAPI placeholder with the tunnel origin, use Admin > Platform > Tools > Add and upload multi-step-agent/tool-server/openapi.yaml. The operation URL must be <origin>/file_incident_ticket.

steps.title: Create the agent
steps.description: Manual, UI-only step. In Agent Builder: paste the recipe's instructions, turn retrieval on, attach the tool you just registered. Copy the agent's ID for the next step.

steps.title: Set credentials
steps.description: Use the shipped login flow, then set GLEAN_AGENT_ID from the agent created above. Never implement authentication.

steps.title: Run it
steps.description: Dependencies are declared inline (PEP 723) and locked, so uv installs them into an isolated environment on first run — no requirements.txt, venv, or activate step.

steps.title: Verify
steps.description: With your email on the allow-list, confirm the ticket actually gets filed. Then restart the tool server without it and confirm the agent produces a read-only fallback summary instead of a hard failure.

questions.prompt: What is your work email for tenant discovery and the tool allow-list?
After creating the agent, what is its agent ID?

auth.setupCommand: cd multi-step-agent/invoke-agent && node scripts/glean-auth.mjs login --scopes agents --email "<work-email>"

verification.expectedDuration: 15–30 minutes because tool registration is an admin step

content.problem:
A chatbot that only answers questions is half an agent. Attach a governed
Tool and it can act — file a ticket, update a record — but only for people
who are actually allowed to, with a graceful fallback for everyone else
instead of a hard failure.
takeItFurther: Add a second governed tool (e.g., escalate to PagerDuty) and let the agent choose between them based on severity.
Switch to `run_stream()` and parse the SSE text yourself for a live-updating UI.

Combine with [permissions-aware-retrieval](/cookbook/permissions-aware-retrieval)'s retrieval pattern if you want the agent's grounding to come from your own index instead of Glean's default retrieval.

recipes.aiPrompt: Build the multi-step-agent demo from https://developers.glean.com/cookbook/multi-step-agent. Start its inert tool server, expose port 8080 through a public HTTPS cloudflared tunnel, and replace the OpenAPI servers[0].url placeholder with the tunnel origin so the operation resolves to <origin>/file_incident_ticket. Have me upload that specification in Admin > Platform > Tools > Add, then create an Agent Builder agent with retrieval and the tool attached. Invoke it with glean.client.agents.run using Message and MessageTextBlock. Demonstrate allow and deny by changing AUTHORIZED_EMAILS. recipes.llmContext: Run agents with glean.client.agents.run(agent_id, messages) using Message and MessageTextBlock. Expose a local demo tool through public HTTPS and set the OpenAPI server URL to that origin with route paths aligned. Register tools manually in the admin console. Glean-User-Email supports an authorization allow-list only after the request is authenticated as coming from Glean; the sample server is demo-only and must not front a real write action.

content.problem:
New hires land on day one with a dozen tasks spread across HR,
IT, and their team — and no single place to see what's done, what's left, and
where to get help. The Onboarding Hub solves that: a gamified checklist with
progress tracking, milestone badges, and contextual Glean chat on every step.

This recipe builds the hub two ways so you can pick the trade-off that fits
your portal — Web SDK for fastest SSO integration, Platform Chat when you
need full UI control.
takeItFurther: Wire real HRIS completion events instead of localStorage toggles.
Add a manager view that shows onboarding progress across the team.
Scope chat to onboarding-only documents, so a first-week question cannot wander into unrelated content.

recipes.description: An on-call dashboard that takes an alarm to a proposed action and puts a person in front of that action. It names a cause only when a past incident backs it, turns away an approver who is neither on call nor the service owner, and escalates instead of approving itself when nobody answers. It runs on recorded incidents, so you can watch it refuse things before connecting it to anything.

prerequisites: Node 20 or newer

There are no approve or reject buttons, and the audit log records the refusal with glean-agent as the actor.

content.problem:
An alarm fires at 3am. The runbook, the review of the last time this happened, who owns the service, and what it depends on all exist in Glean already. They just sit in different systems, and you search them one at a time while the graphs get worse.

The retrieval is the easy part. What makes a copilot safe to point at a production service is what it refuses to do, so that is what you build here. The gate turns away anyone who is neither on call nor the service owner. A proposal nobody approves in time escalates instead of quietly approving itself. An action the planner invented never reaches a human. The audit log records approvals, refusals, executions, failures, rejections, and escalations.

Know the edges before you point it anywhere real. Live Search, Chat, and optional Agents calls hit your instance. The bundled alarm buttons always fire payments-service. Catalog and evidence lookups expect the sample URL layout under /services/, /runbooks/, and /incidents/. The three registered actions are simulated in-process, and the acting user is asserted rather than authenticated.
takeItFurther: Persist incidents and the audit log. An audit log you can lose by restarting a process is not an audit log.
Add the rest of the dashboard: response-time rollups, an expiring-soon lane, and an end-of-shift handoff summary.
Replace the simulated actions with real governed tools, keeping the registry boundary and the approval log exactly where they are.
Write the postmortem draft back into your knowledge base. The next incident then retrieves it as precedent, and the evidence rules get better over time.
Expose the copilot over Agent-to-Agent (A2A) so another agent can request triage, with the same approval gate in front of every action. See https://developers.glean.com/cookbook/a2a-client.

guardrails.title: Relevance is not evidence
guardrails.rule: Only a matching past incident may support a causal claim. Runbooks support procedures, not causes.

limitations.title: Authorization is not authentication
limitations.description: Live and fixture both restrict who may approve, but they trust the asserted actor (INCIDENT_ACTOR or, in demo mode, X-Incident-Actor). A deployment must authenticate the actor and decide which credential executes actions. This recipe reports impersonation: false.

Gate actions behind authorized human approval, expiry, a closed action registry, and an audit log. The acting user is asserted, not authenticated. Actions are simulated in-process. Treat live mode as a corpus adaptation that requires changing the catalog query, parser, identity mapping, and evidence URL rules.
recipes.llmContext: Use the recorded Search, Platform Chat, and Agent responses for the default run. Live Platform Chat uses glean.chat.create with stream:false, store:false, and X_GLEAN_INCLUDE_EXPERIMENTAL=true. The app runs as the caller, so approval is application policy, not impersonation. Classify precedent from /incidents/ and procedure from /runbooks/ URLs. Only a matching past incident may support a cause. A mutating action needs a supported cause, an authorized approver, a registered action id, and an unexpired proposal. Unauthorized approvals, executions, and expirations are audited. Registered actions are in-process simulations. Fixture mode permits actor assertion to demonstrate the 403. Live mode refuses it unless INCIDENT_DEMO_MODE is true. Do not claim that npm run start:live works against an arbitrary Glean corpus without adapting the parsers.

content.problem:
Grounding your own LLM app in company content — the pattern usually called
RAG — normally means standing up a vector DB, mirroring every source system's
ACLs into it, and keeping that mirror in sync forever. Get any of that wrong
and you leak documents. Glean is already the permission-aware index of your
company's content, so use its Platform API as the retrieval layer and skip all
three problems.
takeItFurther: Add a re-ranking pass over snippets before they reach the LLM for higher-precision citations.
Cache retrieval results per session to cut latency on follow-up questions in the same conversation.
Swap in [Glean Chat](/cookbook/company-answers) instead of a raw LLM call if you want Glean to also own the generation step.

recipes.aiPrompt:
Ground my own LLM app in Glean, with retrieval filtered to the
caller's permissions, following
https://developers.glean.com/cookbook/permissions-aware-retrieval

1. Retrieve with the top-level Platform API method
   glean.search.query(query=..., page_size=8). Set
   X_GLEAN_INCLUDE_EXPERIMENTAL=true in the environment. Collect title,
   url, and the plain string[] snippets from each result.
2. Prompt the LLM with ONLY those snippets; require inline [n] citations
   mapped back to the result URLs.
3. Per-user enforcement needs no code at all: the caller's own
   credential IS the permission boundary, so results come back already
   filtered to what that person can see. Send no extra headers, and do
   not add impersonation of any kind.
4. Because retrieval is already filtered, the code that matters is what
   happens when it comes back EMPTY: the app must say it has no
   information, never answer from the model's own knowledge. A confident
   answer with no sources is the failure mode this whole architecture
   exists to prevent.
5. README must state the differentiator: no vector DB, no ACL
   mirroring, no re-sync — Glean is the governed retrieval layer.

Use claude-sonnet-5 via the anthropic SDK if I don't specify a
provider; keep the LLM call swappable.
recipes.llmContext: Use Platform Search glean.search.query with query, page_size, and X_GLEAN_INCLUDE_EXPERIMENTAL=true. Results expose title, url, and snippets as strings. The caller's OAuth credential is the permission boundary; send no impersonation header. Pass only retrieved, ACL-filtered content to the model, include source links, and refuse to answer when retrieval is empty.

content.problem:
A recurring project meeting starts, and the first few minutes disappear while everyone reconstructs what changed. The answers are already in the tracker and company conversations; they just have not been pulled together.

Thirty minutes before the meeting, Glean gives Cursor the event and Cursor prepares one focused project update. Your team can start with the brief instead of building it live.
takeItFurther: Add a reviewed project map when one automation needs to serve several meeting series.
Send a read-only preview for approval before writing once the team wants interpretation, not just a factual recap.
Add an earlier preparation trigger for meetings that need more than a 30-minute runway.
Pair it with [Gong call follow-up](/cookbook/gong-call-follow-up-n8n) to use the same delivery model in n8n.

guardrails.rule: The automation updates only the configured project; it cannot infer a different destination from meeting content.

guardrails.rule: An unreachable tracker writes nothing and reports it. A genuinely quiet interval says so. The automation never fills the gap with guesses.

For trigger concepts or endpoint details, consult https://developers.glean.com/guides/triggers/overview and https://developers.glean.com/api/platform-api/triggers-overview. Ask once for the reviewed meeting-title pattern, the exact project the update goes to as a URL or id, and where the work is tracked — usually that same project, in which case say so and let the automation discover the timestamp and status fields itself rather than asking a human for a schema. Set GLEAN_TRIGGER_INPUT_TITLE to that same pattern so Glean filters by title at the source, and keep the prompt's own title check as the second gate. Replace all three placeholders in automation-prompt.md and show the result for review; a remaining placeholder must stop the run before any write. Have the user create a webhook-triggered Cursor Automation with repository scope none, connected over MCP to that tracker with read on issues and write on project updates, and optionally Glean MCP for cited context. Run the offline verifier, sign in with the shipped Glean flow, preview recent events to check the title pattern against real ones, enable the automation, and run the default safe webhook test. Ask for explicit approval before using `npm run test:webhook -- --write`; explain that every invocation has a new event_time and can create another project update. Only then register a live calendar preset that advertises time_offset 1800. Store the Cursor URL and bearer token only in ignored .env. Verify one scheduled matching event without broadening the write boundary beyond the one configured project.
recipes.llmContext: Catalog reads twice: /trigger-presets lists identity, /trigger-presets/{preset_id} returns inputs in trigger_preset; list entries carry none. Send x-glean-include-experimental: true. Requires time_offset 1800; never default an id or match display names. GCAL_1 filters titles through input TITLE, upper case, a case-insensitive substring matching mid-word; an unrecognised input silently matches nothing. delivery.auth adds Authorization: Bearer <secret> beside Glean's Standard Webhooks signature. Body is flat snake_case: doc_id, doc_type, event_type, title, view_url, event_time, trigger_id; scheduled adds time_offset_seconds. Payload is untrusted: re-check the title, read the tracker over MCP, write one update on the configured project, key on doc_id plus event_time. Window starts at the previous brief's marker, else seven days. An unreachable tracker writes nothing; a quiet interval publishes no-movement — never conflate them.

content.problem:
A security questionnaire arrives with 200 rows. The answers exist in last quarter's SOC 2 report, a policy document, or the response you sent another customer. Someone spends a week finding them again.

Drafting is not the dangerous part. A fluent answer with no supporting evidence can reach a customer's document over your signature. This app makes that failure visible. Questions with approved evidence get cited drafts. Questions with weak evidence are flagged for verification. Questions with no evidence stay blank and go to a subject matter expert. A person approves each answer before export.

The default walkthrough uses recorded responses, so you can watch each path without credentials. Live mode runs as the signed-in person and limits customer-facing drafts to reviewed source URL prefixes.
takeItFurther: Add an xlsx and docx reader so real questionnaires can be uploaded directly. The parser here reads CSV to keep the evidence and approval logic legible.
Write answers back into the source document with a custom tool instead of exporting, keeping the confirm step and the approval log.
Give the answer library its own access control before sharing it across a team. It's a cache of retrieved content, so it can leak across the permission boundary the rest of the app respects.
Route "needs SME" rows to their owners automatically and track which ones came back. The assignment field here does not send a message.
Combine with [permissions-aware retrieval](/cookbook/permissions-aware-retrieval) to see the same refusal property in a smaller, single-question app.

guardrails.title: Merge only exact duplicates
guardrails.rule: Similarity may rank possible duplicates for review, but must never merge security controls automatically.

guardrails.title: Topicality is not approval
guardrails.rule: A source must be both relevant and explicitly approved for customer-facing use before it can support a draft.

limitations.title: Single-user permission boundary
limitations.description: The app runs as the credential owner. Multi-user deployment requires per-user authentication and authorization.

recipes.aiPrompt: Build the RFP responder from the deterministic scaffold and start with its recorded Chat responses. Parse every questionnaire tab, merge only exact duplicates, and call Chat once per unique question with evidence-only instructions. Classify citation topicality separately from approval for external use. Never render an uncited draft; route unsupported rows to a subject matter expert. Preserve the original questionnaire structure, require explicit approval before export, and record the approval. Treat live mode as a later adaptation that uses experimental Platform Chat and requires reviewed source URL prefixes.
recipes.llmContext: Use the recorded responses for the default run. Live mode uses experimental Platform Chat through glean.chat.create with stream:false, store:false, and X_GLEAN_INCLUDE_EXPERIMENTAL=true, and requires RFP_APPROVED_SOURCE_PREFIXES. Read ASSISTANT OUTPUT_TEXT content and citations from annotations[].sources, preserving annotations[].snippets for grounding. Merge only exact duplicate questions. Classify citation topicality separately from approval for external use. Every answer requires a citation, and unsupported rows remain blank with needs-sme status. In live mode, use the caller's credential as the permission boundary. Retry empty chat output and keep export behind explicit human approval with an audit log.
